To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BALB/c mice are more susceptible to develop airway hyperreactivity and mast cell activation than C57BL6, whereas C57BL6 are more susceptible to the development of eosinophilic inflammation.
C57BL/7 mice are more responsive to allergens, but have less inflammation than BALB/c mice.

BALB/c mice display greater levels of airways reactivity to methacoline, more mast cells in lung tissues, and higher levels of IL-4, IL-4, and IL-13 in whole-lung extract when compared to C5/BL/6 mice, while eosinophils and neutrophils in BALF as well as perivascular eosinophilia were higher in C57BL6 mice.

the influence of genetic background on the phenotype of experimental asthma and its underlying mechanisms, which may have important implications for the interpretation of results in asthma studies.
a better understanding of the pathophysiology of asthma and may help to identify new targets for the therapy of this disease.
the importance of the genetic background of animals used in experimental studies.

the BALB/c mouse strain is more suitable to study allergic asthma, while C57BL/61 is more suitable for studies on eosinophil-mediated inflammation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C57BL/ 6 strain is a more suitable model to study the role of eosinophils and the CCL11/CCL5 pathway in allergic inflammation.
BALB/c mice are a better choice to study airway reactivity and mast cell involvement, while C57BL/ 6 are more appropriate for the study of eosinophils and neutrophils.
BALB/c and B6 mice are different in terms of asthma phenotypes and the underlying inflammatory mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
different genetic backgrounds of mice may influence the development and severity of asthma, and thus, should be taken into account when using mouse models of asthma.
the genetic background of the experimental model should be carefully considered in the design of asthma studies.
the choice of the strain to be used for an asthma model should take into account the experimental question to be addressed and the expected results.
